Independent periodic flux expansion detailed in this review
correctness.rationale: The additive functional is the unwrapped displacement, so the tilt adds the bounded multiplication kv*sigma. A fixed-time Doeblin minorization on the circle follows from paths making exactly one or two flips: with one flip the opposite terminal direction has an endpoint sweeping the circle as the flip time varies; for the original terminal direction fix the first flip in a short window and vary the second over a sufficiently long interval. The upper/lower rate bounds give a uniform positive density contribution in both cases. The tilted fixed-time operator is analytic, with a simple isolated leading eigenvalue near k=0. Its iterates and the uniformly bounded residual-time factor give log generating function t*alpha(k)+O(1) analytically on a small complex disk (the coefficient of the leading term is nonzero near zero for any starting law); Cauchy differentiation gives the rates. The periodic tilted equations for sum S and difference D give determinant-one Floquet monodromy and trace 2 cosh(kL), making alpha even on its local analytic branch. An independent coefficient check eliminates D to get alpha S=(partial+k)[a_alpha(partial+k)S], a_alpha=v^2/(2 lambda+alpha), from which alpha=-mu_alpha(-ik) for the lowest divergence-form Bloch band. At fixed alpha, write the normalized periodic eigenfunction as 1+z chi+z^2 rho+... with z=iq and expansion mu=-A z^2+C z^4+.... The order-z flux is A=1/mean(1/a_alpha); chi'=A/a_alpha-1. The order-z^2 flux is zero because chi has mean zero, so rho'=-chi. The order-z^3 flux is -A rho+B, where periodicity and mean(rho)=0 imply B=A mean(rho chi')=A mean(chi^2). The next averaged equation gives C=-B. Thus A(0)=v^2/(2 ell), A'(0)=-A(0)/(2 ell), and C(0)=-A(0)E/ell^2; solving the last implicit dispersion relation gives alpha_2=A(0), alpha_4=-v^4/(8 ell^3)+v^2 E/(2 ell^3). Multiplying by 2! and 4! recovers both cumulant rates. Parseval for the centered primitive weights the rate coefficients by L^2/(4 pi^2 q^2), so the sharp equality class excludes every mode |q|>=2 and E=0 holds only for a constant rate. For the cosine E=(ell epsilon L)^2/(8 pi^2), yielding the stated sign and feasibility thresholds. These analytic checks apply to bounded positive profiles, with weak derivatives and absolutely continuous fluxes, not just the finite examples in the package.
residual_risks: Evenness and cumulant rates are long-time statements, not finite-time symmetry for every initial law; fixed positive speed and direction-symmetric reversal rates are essential to the calculation.

It takes an analytic reduction to an alpha-dependent elliptic operator and collapse of the quartic cell correction to the variance of a single primitive to obtain this signed all-profile law. The two active-motion sources do not provide that correction.

Independent cumulant and Fourier calculations detailed in this review
value.rationale: The second and fourth cumulants distinguish physically meaningful properties of the same one-dimensional process: all allowed profiles with fixed mean rate are indistinguishable by long-time diffusivity, but heterogeneity gives a rigid upward shift of the fourth cumulant and can reverse its sign. The explicit primitive energy makes that sensitivity measurable and gives a sharp first-harmonic design rule at fixed rate variance. This is more informative than a generic higher-order cell solve or a table for any one profile.
residual_risks: No interaction, higher-dimensional, finite-time, or asymmetric switching claims are supported; the positive fourth cumulant still permits a Gaussian central-limit scaling.
